chapter: Los Angeles bands and theater pits, 1927-30
title: Leon René's band at Belmont and Culver City
summary: In 1928 he joins Leon René's band at the open-air dance, then a reopened Culver City spot that fails against Frank Sebastian's club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: In 1928 I joined Leon René's band, also at Belmon.
I think Mr. Leon René is the composer of that song, 'When the Swallows Come Back to Capistrano'.
He had a brother by the name of Otis René.
That's right, and a cousin named Sam Beaumon; he had the drugstore.

I stayed with Leon from June to the holidays. We worked at the open air dance until it closed, then we went out to Spie'Iman's Nightingale (phonetic spelling) in Culver City. It had been closed and he
tried to reopen it and we went to the re-opening because he was bucking Frank Sebastian next door, and he had Miss Carolyn Snowden's review.
I think Miss Snowden was an outstanding woman musician at that time?
No, she was just a show producer. You're talking about the other Snow-- Valaida.
No, no. One was Snow and the other was Snowden.

Of course that job didn't last, he didn't make it go and so Leon didn't have much work and so the last job I had with him was on New Year's Eve, 1928/ After that I didn't play with him anymore because he didn't have any work.
